page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 2.0 GB of system memory. Powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%, alongside average single-threaded performance in gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core evaluations. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance is limited. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, while memory bandwidth, database operations, and Redis SET operations register in the lowest 10% tier.

Due to its low memory allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU and weak multi-threaded scaling, the n2d-highcpu-2 presents clear resource constraints. It is highly cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have minimal memory footprints. This instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, and simple utility scripts. It is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or high-throughput web serving.
